To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

site councils are more likely to be perceived to be effective if the councils are given sufficient authority and capacity to carry out their responsibilities and if council practices are oriented toward decision-making and positive communication.
site councils with a strong focus on decision-making and positive communication are likely to be perceived as more effective than site councils without these characteristics.
site councils with greater capacity, authority and decision focus, and more positive communication are more likely to perceive that they have made a positive impact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the embedded logic of the theory of action that connects the resources available to site councils with the perceived outcomes of their efforts to improve the quality of education in the schools.
the relationships among the resources, the practices, and the outcomes of site councils.
the question of how to build effective site councils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

site-based management councils can have a positive impact on the quality of school life and the educational process if they have sufficient resources, if they use those resources to focus on decision-making and to communicate in positive ways, and if they are able to translate those resources into the authority to act.
site councils with more resources are likely to have more effective practices, and that site councils with effective practices will have more positive outcomes.
site-based management is an organizational form that can be effective, but that it is not necessarily effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important factor in site-based management is the quality of the communication and decision-making processes.
site council outcomes are a function of the support and practices of site councils.

the more a school site team is provided with capacity to do the work and the authority to do the work, the better the team is able to communicate and focus on decisions that are important to the school.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the support and practices of councils are not independent of each other; they are linked by a chain of causality.
the quality and effectiveness of site councils is not simply a function of the support provided to councils, but rather is a function of how that support is translated into practice.

the support for site-based management is not only important in itself, but also in the sense that the support is likely to have a significant indirect effect on the perceived effectiveness of site-based management.
